archetype.name: Improviser (scramble-heavy)
archetype.definition: A quarterback who holds the ball, waits for something to open downfield, and turns broken pockets into first downs with his legs. That makes him productive and leaves him exposed to pressure.

report.headline: Two games of real accuracy progress, now stalled by a strained hamstring
report.take:
Williams is in his third season. The arc so far runs from a rough rookie year (-0.03 EPA per play, 40th of 60) to a functional 2025 (0.086, 27th of 63) to a 0.292 per dropback this year that ranks 7th of 43. That last number rests on two games and 70 dropbacks before the hamstring took him out of the lineup. Case Keenum started Weeks 3 and 4 and Tyson Bagent started Week 5. The Week 6 trip to Atlanta is officially in doubt: the site lists him Out, and Ben Johnson said only that it is "going to be close."

The two games point in opposite directions. Carolina, now 21st in defensive EPA, gave him 21 of 29 for 269 yards, 18.6 passing EPA, 65 rushing yards and two rushing scores. Minnesota, now 1st, held him to 138 yards on 26 attempts and -1.0 passing EPA. In that game his intended air yards fell to 3.9 as he checked down against 21 blitzes and a 40.6% pressure rate. Average the two and you get a good season line. Neither game alone describes him. In one-score situations, 55 of his 70 plays, he ran a more modest 0.134 EPA. That is closer to his true level than the headline 0.292.

The most interesting signal is accuracy. He finished his first two seasons below expectation in completion percentage (CPOE of -3.5 in 2025, 49th of 63), and his bad-throw rate ranked 52nd or worse both years. This year his CPOE is +5.5 and his bad-throw rate is 10.9%, 15th of 36. Fifty-five attempts can't prove a change, but it is the right direction. The usual explanation, a second year in Johnson's system, is plausible. What hasn't changed is the style. His time to throw has climbed from 2.92 to 3.20 to 3.42 seconds, and he is pressured on 40% of dropbacks, the highest rate among 36 charted quarterbacks.

The style mostly pays. Scrambles make up 14.3% of his dropbacks, and they have averaged 0.914 EPA with six first downs on ten tries. That is the fuel under the Carolina game and the reason the Minnesota game wasn't worse. It is also why a hamstring strain matters more for him than for a pocket passer. The first games back, whenever they come, may show a quarterback who has to stand in and throw against pressure he would normally escape.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay for the pressure
strengths.body: Ten scrambles have produced 86 yards, six first downs and nearly a point of EPA each. That is the payoff for how long he holds the ball. He has ranked 7th in quarterback rushing yards in both prior seasons, so the skill is established. How fast it returns depends on the hamstring.

strengths.title: Accuracy finally above expectation
strengths.body: A +5.5 CPOE (8th of 43) and a bad-throw rate in the middle of the pack replace two years of below-expectation accuracy. The sample is 55 attempts, and Week 2 was -5.6. The likely truth is better than 2025 but not this good.

strengths.title: A real year-over-year efficiency climb
strengths.body: His EPA has moved from negative as a rookie to above average in 2025 to top-10 this year. Along the way his pressure-to-sack rate fell from 43.5% to 15.9%. The rookie sack problem was solved, which is the most durable sign of growth on his record.

concerns.title: A leg injury to a legs-dependent quarterback
concerns.body: His hamstring status is the biggest variable on the card. Johnson was non-committal and the site lists him Out for Week 6. Designed runs were already a loser (-0.553 EPA, 60% stuffed), so his rushing value lives almost entirely in scrambles. Scrambling is the thing a strained hamstring takes away first.

concerns.title: Most-pressured quarterback in the league
concerns.body: He is pressured on 40% of dropbacks (36th of 36) and sacked on 8.3% (34th of 43). Part of that is his 3.42-second time to throw, so it is the price of the extension game rather than a protection collapse. Even so, it turned the Minnesota game into a 3-9 loss, and the price goes up if he can't escape.

concerns.title: Third-down numbers that won't hold
concerns.body: Converting 58.8% of third downs at an average of 8.3 yards to go, with 0.613 EPA on those plays, is an unsustainable clip on 17 plays. Expect it to regress toward his overall efficiency, which will pull his EPA ranking down with it.

trend.note: A 37-point fantasy game against a weak Carolina defense was followed by a 7.7-point dud against the league's top defense. He then missed three straight starts with the hamstring, so there is no recent form to read.

nextGame.headline: Status in doubt, and Atlanta takes away the deep shots
nextGame.body:
Atlanta's defense ranks 7th in EPA and 3rd in success rate. It allows little through the air: 8th in pass EPA, 8th in explosive-pass rate and 5th on deep throws. That shuts down the downfield payoff that drove his Week 1. Quarterbacks do pile up volume against the Falcons, who allow 266 yards a game (23rd) and the strongest pass-rate-over-norm in the league. That looks more like a defense opponents choose to throw on than one that gets beaten. The Falcons hit the quarterback often (6th) but finish few sacks (22nd). A healthy Williams would like that mix, because it is pressure he can escape. On a strained hamstring it is just pressure.

Availability dominates. Williams is listed Out and his coach called a return "close." If he is cleared, expect a cautious plan that limits his scrambling. Backup back Kyle Monangai (41% of snaps) is out, leaving more of the backfield work to D'Andre Swift. On Atlanta's side, Za'Darius Smith (concussion) is out, which thins the edge rotation. Cornerback C.J. Henderson (groin) is questionable. Michael Penix Jr. is questionable with ribs, and a compromised Penix would weaken a pass offense that already ranks 27th. That would make it easier for Chicago to play a low-risk game script.

keyMatchups.title: Downfield game versus a top-5 deep defense
keyMatchups.body: His seven deep attempts produced 0.682 EPA, a large share of his efficiency. Atlanta allows -0.08 EPA on deep passes, 5th best. Expect a shorter, more possession-based plan than Week 1.

keyMatchups.title: Pressure that hits but rarely sacks
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's high hit rate and low sack rate mean pocket breakdowns without finishes. That usually invites scrambles from a quarterback like him. Whether his hamstring allows him to take them decides whether this matchup helps him or hurts him.

keyMatchups.title: Kalif Raymond against the WR2 soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Raymond has been his most productive target, at 0.833 EPA on 14 targets. Atlanta allows 0.51 EPA per play to opposing WR2s (25th of 32) while holding WR1s in check, so the secondary option is where the openings have been.

nextGame.watch: Whether he is cleared, and if so, whether he scrambles early or stays in the pocket.

restOfSeason.body:
Assuming he returns soon, the baseline is somewhere between his 2025 season and this two-game burst. The accuracy gains should partly stick, but a +5.5 CPOE on 55 attempts will drift toward zero. The third-down conversion rate and the efficiency built while leading big will fade. The pressure rate will stay high because his time to throw is part of his game. His sack avoidance was strong in 2025 and should keep that from becoming a disaster.

The rushing line is the most fragile piece. Thirty-plus rushing yards a game depends on scrambling, and a strained hamstring may cap that for a few weeks. Chicago's offense held up at 12th in EPA with backups, so the system will give him a decent floor when he's back.
swingFactors: Hamstring recovery and whether his scrambling returns
Whether the CPOE gain holds over a full sample
Protection against a league-worst pressure rate

confidence.note: Two games and 70 dropbacks, then three missed starts; return date and mobility uncertain.
